newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Adtranz says wins 1.15 bln SKR British order.
newsitem.headline: Adtranz says wins 1.15 bln SKR British order.

text.p: International railway systems company Adtranz said on Thursday it had won an order worth 1.15 billion crowns ($150 million) from Connex Rail Ltd in Britain for 30 four-wagon multiple unit trains of the Electrostar model.
Adtranz, which is jointly owned by ABB and Daimler-Benz , said the contract included an option for another 800 wagons. ($ = 7.683 Swedish Crowns)
The option, if exercised, could be worth a further five billion crowns, Staffan Hakanson, managing director for Adtranz Sweden, told Reuters.
"It would over five billion crowns, there is no doubt about that," Hakanson said.
Adtranz said in a statement that the trains would be made at its plant in Derby, England.
"They will be furnished with the latest generation electrical traction equipment with IGBT from Adtranz Sweden," the statement said.
The traction equipment give the operators lower operating costs due to less weight, increased reliability and simpler maintenance.
Adtranz Sweden's part of the order is worth over 200 million crown and will keep its plant at Vasteras in Sweden busy for two years.
"Over the next few years there will be a lot of contract concluded in the privatised market in England," said Hakanson.

"This means Adtranz Sweden, which is responsible for electrical traction equipment in the intermediate range for Adtranz, has good possibilities to supply large volumes of traction equipment to our subsidiary in England."
Adtranz Sweden has an annual turnover of three billion crowns and 1,500 staff while the Adtranz group has an annual turnover of 28 billion crowns and 22,000 employees.
